# Story 07 — Admin Movie Management (Story: 6)

## Prerequisites

- Story that introduced `AdminLayoutComponent`, `admin.guard.ts`, and the `/admin` route shell must be completed (see `src/app/features/admin/admin-layout/` and `src/app/features/admin/admin.routes.ts`, both already present in the repo tree).
- Story that introduced Hall Management (admin-dashboard intake `5`, backend-issue-5 "Admin Hall Management") must be completed and merged. The movie feature **must follow the same structural pattern** already implemented for halls under `src/app/features/admin/halls/` (`hall-list`, `hall-create`, `hall-edit`, `hall-details`, `hall-form`, `hall.service.ts`, `hall.models.ts`, `hall-error.util.ts`). Locate the corresponding sibling plan file under `.squad/plans/admin-dashboard/` (the plan whose title references Hall Management / issue `5`) and mirror its component decomposition, service shape, and error-handling conventions for movies.
- `src/app/core/auth/auth.interceptor.ts` and `src/app/core/auth/admin.guard.ts` must already be wired into `app.config.ts` / `app.routes.ts` so that admin API calls carry the auth token and non-admin users are redirected — confirm this is true before starting (both files already exist per the repo tree).
- Coordinate with whoever owns the "Movies" customer-facing feature (`src/app/features/movies/`, using `src/app/features/movies/services/movie.service.ts` and `src/app/features/movies/models/movie.model.ts`) — this story must **not** modify the customer-facing movie service/model; it introduces a **separate, admin-only** service and model set under `src/app/features/admin/movies/` so that inactive movies never leak into the customer listing (`GET /api/movies` for admin vs. whatever endpoint the customer feature calls — verify the customer feature already filters to active movies only and do not change that call).

## Story Goal

Enable an authenticated administrator to:

1. View a list of all movies (active and inactive) at `/admin/movies`, with title, genre, duration, release date, language, and active/inactive status clearly shown, plus row actions (View / Edit / Deactivate / Activate).
2. Create a new movie at `/admin/movies/create` via a validated reactive form, submitted to `POST /api/movies`.
3. Edit an existing movie at `/admin/movies/{id}/edit`, pre-populated from `GET /api/movies/{id}`, submitted to `PUT /api/movies/{id}`.
4. View full movie details at `/admin/movies/{id}`, including a safe (non-embedded) link/button to open the trailer URL if present.
5. Deactivate a movie (`PATCH /api/movies/{id}/deactivate`) and activate a movie (`PATCH /api/movies/{id}/activate`), each gated by a confirmation dialog, with the UI updated in place (no removal from the list).

Out of scope for this story: any change to the customer-facing movie browsing feature (`src/app/features/movies/`) beyond confirming it is unaffected; any change to the screening-creation UI (`src/app/features/admin/screenings/`) beyond noting that it must only offer active movies — implementing that filter is deferred to the screening-creation story unless that story is already merged, in which case coordinate to ensure the admin movie service exposes an `isActive` field it can filter on. Backend authorization enforcement is out of scope; the frontend only reacts to `401`/`403` responses.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Current behavior (halls precedent):** the halls feature already implements list/create/edit/details plus a state-toggle action (see `hall-list.component.ts`, `hall-details.component.ts`); movies must follow the identical interaction pattern rather than inventing a new one.
- **New behavior for movies:**
  - Two distinct state-changing actions instead of one toggle: **Deactivate** (`PATCH /api/movies/{id}/deactivate`) and **Activate** (`PATCH /api/movies/{id}/activate`) — the list/details UI must show exactly one of these two actions depending on the movie's current `isActive` value, both behind a confirmation dialog.
  - Deactivating a movie must **never remove it** from the admin list/history — only its status badge and available action change.
  - Inactive movies must be **visually distinct** (e.g., a muted row style and an "Inactive" badge) in the admin list and details view, consistent with (but not necessarily identical to) whatever visual convention `hall-list.component.html`/`.css` uses for inactive/deleted halls.
  - Trailer URL must never be rendered as an `<iframe>` or embedded player — only as an external link (`<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` or a button that opens the URL), consistent with "do not attempt to embed arbitrary URLs."

```ts
export type MovieGenre = 'Comedy' | 'Action' | 'Drama' | 'Fantasy';

  description: string;

  genre: MovieGenre | '';
  duration: number | null;
  releaseDate: string;
  language: string;
  description: string;
  actors: string;
  trailerUrl: string;
}

  title: string;
  genre: string;
  duration: number;
  releaseDate: string;
  language: string;
  description: string;
  actors: string;
  trailerUrl?: string;
}

```

**Create directory/component: `src/app/features/admin/movies/movie-form/movie-form.component.ts`, `.html`, `.css`**

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty movie list** — `GET /api/movies` returns `[]`: `movie-list.component` must render the empty-state message, not a blank table. Enforced in the list component's template conditional (mirror `hall-list.component.html`'s empty-state block).
- **Duration of zero or negative** — form must reject via `Validators.min(1)` on the `duration` control in `movie-form.component.ts`; the submit button stays disabled and no request is sent to `POST /api/movies` or `PUT /api/movies/{id}`.
- **Invalid trailer URL** (e.g. `"not-a-url"`) — rejected client-side by `validUrlValidator()` before submission; the field shows an inline error and the form remains invalid. Empty trailer URL is valid (field is optional per the intake's "Trailer URL must be a valid URL when provided").
- **401 Unauthorized on any movie API call** — mapped by `movie-error.util.ts` to a friendly "session expired / please log in" message; do not attempt automatic navigation from the service itself unless `hall.service.ts`/`auth.interceptor.ts` already establishes a global 401-redirect convention, in which case follow that convention exactly (verify in `auth.interceptor.ts`).
- **403 Forbidden** — non-admin token (should be unreachable given `admin.guard.ts`, but the API is the source of truth) — mapped to a "not authorized" message, no destructive UI state change on deactivate/activate failures.
- **409 Conflict on deactivate** (e.g. movie is scheduled in upcoming active screenings, if the backend enforces this) — mapped to a specific "cannot deactivate" message in `movie-error.util.ts`; the movie's `isActive` state in the list/details view must **not** be optimistically flipped until the API call actually succeeds.
- **404 Not Found on edit/details** (movie deleted or bad id) — `movie-edit.component.ts`/`movie-details.component.ts` must show an error state with no form/details rendered, and offer navigation back to `/admin/movies`.
- **Confirmation dialog dismissed** — clicking Deactivate/Activate then cancelling the confirmation must make **zero** API calls and leave the row/details state unchanged.
- **Concurrent deactivate/activate from two admin sessions** — the frontend has no realtime sync; simply reflect the last successful response for the current session's list, and rely on the `409`/`404` handling above if a stale action is retried against an already-changed movie.
- **Genre value not in `MOVIE_GENRES`** (e.g. backend adds a new genre not yet in the frontend enum) — flag this as an **open uncertainty**: the intake says "The UI should provide the genres supported by the backend," but no `GET /api/genres`-style endpoint is documented. The frontend hardcodes `MOVIE_GENRES` for now; document this limitation in a code comment in `movie.models.ts` as a known follow-up.

## Verification Steps

1. **Frontend builds:** `ng build` in the project root (`.`).
2. **Frontend unit tests:** `ng test --watch=false` in the project root, confirming all new specs under `src/app/features/admin/movies/` and `src/app/shared/validators/` pass, and no existing spec (`halls`, `auth`, `app.routes`) regresses.
3. **Manual smoke (dev server):** `ng serve`, log in as an admin user, navigate to `/admin/movies`, create a movie, edit it, view its details, deactivate it (confirm the dialog appears and the row updates without disappearing), then reactivate it.
4. **Regression:** run the full `ng test --watch=false` suite once more after all files are added to confirm the admin guard/auth interceptor specs still pass unmodified.

## Done Criteria

- [ ] Administrator can view the movie list at `/admin/movies` with loading, empty, and error states.
- [ ] Administrator can create a movie at `/admin/movies/create` via `POST /api/movies`.
- [ ] Administrator can edit a movie at `/admin/movies/{id}/edit` via `GET`/`PUT /api/movies/{id}`.
- [ ] Administrator can view movie details at `/admin/movies/{id}`, including a safe external trailer link when present.
- [ ] Administrator can deactivate a movie (`PATCH /api/movies/{id}/deactivate`) and activate a movie (`PATCH /api/movies/{id}/activate`), each behind a confirmation dialog, without removing it from the list.
- [ ] Genre is selected from the fixed `MOVIE_GENRES` list in the form.
- [ ] Duration ≤ 0 is rejected client-side; form cannot be submitted.
- [ ] Malformed trailer URL is rejected client-side; empty trailer URL is accepted.
- [ ] Title, genre, duration, release date, language, and description are all required client-side.
- [ ] Inactive movies are visually distinguishable in both list and details views.
- [ ] `401`/`403`/`404`/`409`/`400`/`500` responses from any movie endpoint show a user-friendly message via `movie-error.util.ts`.
- [ ] The customer-facing movie feature (`src/app/features/movies/`) is untouched by this story.
- [ ] All new and existing unit tests pass (`ng test --watch=false`), and `ng build` succeeds.
